Ăgȳrĭum , i, n.,
I.a very old town in Sicily, not far from Enna, the birthplace of Diodorus Siculus, now S. Filippo d'Argiro, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 28.—Hence, Ăgyrĭnen-ses , ium, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 28; or Ăgyrī-ni , orum, inhabitants of Agyrium, Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 91.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
